done_when: When forge merge merges a story's last task, it writes the story's done record in that same merge, from an outcome given with --outcome or taken from the story's title, and forge story done is only needed to change that outcome later; no separate pull request. New and existing repos: same in any repo on this release; stories already marked done are untouched. One command-level test: merging the last task leaves the story done with no extra pull request.

findings.body: If a story's final two independent tasks merge concurrently, both commands can inspect an origin/default snapshot where the other task is still unmerged. Both then omit the completion record, even though GitHub subsequently merges both pull requests successfully. The fetch occurs in `src/forge/repo.py:174`, before the checks wait; this predicate has no synchronization with sibling merges. Afterwards, `src/forge/story.py:630–643` finds every task merged but no completion marker, so the board and `forge next` still require `forge story done`. This affects both direct merge calls and `forge land` through `src/forge/land.py:81`. Coordinate sibling merges and refresh their merge state before deciding which merge records completion.
findings.title: Preserve completion when sibling tasks merge concurrently

why: Recording that a story is done opens a separate fix and pull request just to write one record, costing a full review and CI run per story
